stem.text: The volume of water in a reservoir is modeled by \( W(t) = \ln{\left(t + 1 \right)} + 3 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{3} \right)} + 28 \) million gallons, where t is measured in days for \( 0 \le t \le 4 \). Using a calculator, find \( W'(1.5) \), the rate at which the amount is changing at time t = 1.5. Show the setup for the calculation, give the value correct to three decimal places, and include units.

worked_solution.text: The quantity asked for is the derivative of W at t = 1.5: \( W'(1.5) = \left. \frac{d}{dt}\left(\ln{\left(t + 1 \right)} + 3 \sin{\left(\frac{t^{2}}{3} \right)} + 28\right) \right|_{t=1.5} \).
With the calculator in radian mode, the numerical derivative at t = 1.5 gives \( W'(1.5) \) approximately 2.595 million gallons per day.

options.derivation: the numerical derivative taken with the calculator in degree mode, so the sine reads its argument in degrees
the derivative reported to two places instead of three
the function value W(1.5) reported in place of the derivative value
